input:
This review examines the cost of a regional delivery route, whose total cost is $510k per year. The route covers 394 km per trip at a carrier rate of $1.99 per km, so each trip costs, as a derived figure, $784.06. Over a year the route runs 651 trips, and the per-trip cost taken over that number of trips produces the annual total.

The figures are drawn from carrier invoices covering the last 12 months, so the annual cost records what was actually paid, rather than an estimate projected from a published tariff. Empty running is included in the trip count: trips made without a load are counted alongside loaded trips, so the annual figure covers loaded and empty kilometres together.

Because the total is assembled from a rate per kilometre, a distance per trip and a number of trips, the annual cost can be moved through any one of these components: a change in the negotiated rate would alter the cost of every kilometre, a change in the route would alter the distance on each trip, and a change in the schedule would alter the number of trips run. What the review reports, however, is the position as invoiced over the period covered, with each component standing at the value it actually took during that period.
target:
A regional delivery route costs $510k per year. The route runs 394 km per trip at $1.99 per km, a derived $784.06 per trip, over 651 trips per year. The annual figure is the per-trip cost taken over the trip count, and it is built from carrier invoices for the last 12 months, so it records what was paid rather than what a tariff card would predict.

Empty running is included in the trip count. The count is a count of journeys made, loaded or not, and the distance is the distance of the route as driven. The annual cost covers loaded and empty kilometres together, and a reduction in empty running lowers the trip count or the distance per trip without any change in the rate per kilometre. The rate, the distance and the count are the three components the figure contains, and the invoice base fixes each at last year's value: a renegotiated rate changes the cost per kilometre, a route change changes the distance, and a schedule change changes the count.

No other cost of the route is in the figure. The total is transport as invoiced, at the stated rate and distance, over the stated year, and it changes only when one of its three components changes.
